voice_performance.performance_intent: Bright, playful explainer narrator delivering a mystery-and-reveal arc — confident, never condescending.
voice_performance.energy_curve: Punchy curious hook, steady build through the physics, a beat of drama at the violet reveal, warm settled close.
voice_performance.pause_policy: Short pause after the hook question; pause before 'But violet waves are even shorter' (the reversal); pause before the final takeaway line.

provider_notes.piper: Offline voice with no emotion controls — expressiveness comes from punctuation, short sentences, and per-section generation. Em-dashes and periods create natural pauses. Generate each section as a separate audio file.

sections.label: Hook
sections.text: Violet light scatters through our atmosphere even more than blue. So why isn't the sky violet?
sections.speaker_directions: Confident, intriguing. Land 'more than blue' cleanly, brief beat, then the question with rising curiosity.

delivery_cues.delivery_note: The question is the whole video's promise — let it hang.

sections.label: Setup — kill the myth
sections.text: First, forget the ocean myth. The sky is just as blue over a desert. The real story starts when sunlight slams into air molecules and scatters. But not all colors scatter equally.
sections.speaker_directions: Brisk dismissal of the myth, then shift to storytelling mode on 'The real story starts'.

delivery_cues.delivery_note: 'But not all colors scatter equally' is the bridge — slow slightly.
delivery_cues.provider_text: First, forget the ocean myth. The sky is just as blue over a desert. The real story starts when sunlight slams into air molecules, and scatters. But not all colors scatter equally.

sections.label: Build — the fourth-power law
sections.text: Lord Rayleigh showed that scattering explodes as wavelength shrinks. By wavelength to the fourth power. Short blue waves scatter roughly six times more than long red ones. Blue bounces everywhere. Red flies straight through.
sections.speaker_directions: Precise and building. Punch 'fourth power' and 'six times'. The last two short sentences should feel like a snap conclusion.

delivery_cues.delivery_note: Keep the two closing fragments crisp — they mirror the visual split.

sections.label: Climax — the violet paradox resolved
sections.text: But violet waves are even shorter. They scatter most of all. Three things save the blue. The sun emits less violet. The upper atmosphere absorbs some of it. And your eyes barely notice the rest. Blue cones win.
sections.speaker_directions: Dramatic beat before 'But'. Deliver the three reasons as a clean list with micro-pauses. 'Blue cones win' lands like a verdict.

delivery_cues.delivery_note: This is the aha section — the sample gate section. Each of the three reasons gets its own breath.

sections.label: Landing — sunset payoff
sections.text: So the sky's color is decided partly in the air, and partly inside your head. And at sunset, the same physics over a longer path paints the whole sky red.
sections.speaker_directions: Warm and settled. Slow slightly on 'partly inside your head'. The sunset line is a gift, not a lecture.

delivery_cues.delivery_note: Final line should feel like the camera pulling back.
